documents: Published paper (PDF): Eibl et al. 2022, Performance of a Rotational Sensor to Decipher Volcano Seismic Signals on Etna, Italy, JGR Solid Earth 127, e2021JB023617

entry.evidence: In 2019 we recorded the full seismic wavefield using a newly developed 3C rotational sensor co-located with a 3C traditional seismometer on Etna, Italy.

steps.action: Deployed a newly developed 3C blueSeis-3A rotational sensor co-located with a 3C Trillium Compact seismometer on one granitic base plate at RS1 on Etna for one month, oriented with a fiber-optic gyro compass.
steps.quote: using a newly developed 3C rotational sensor co-located with a 3C traditional seismometer on Etna

steps.action: Took up published single-station rotational back-azimuth and phase-velocity methods (Wassermann et al. 2020; Hadziioannou et al. 2012).
steps.quote: The back azimuth is estimated based on the similarity of the rotation rates measured around the horizontal axes

steps.action: Posed the aim of comparing the rotational sensor with the co-located seismometer, and the 6C station with the INGV-OE network, for VT events, LP events and tremor.
steps.quote: We compare the performance of (a) the rotational sensor with respect to the co-located seismometer

steps.action: Designed event detection as the intersection of STA/LTA and template cross-correlation catalogs, built separately for each sensor, with set filter bands, windows and thresholds.
steps.quote: We consider only events included in both catalogs in the final event catalog of the seismometer.

steps.action: Varied STA/LTA and cross-correlation thresholds, SNR window lengths (1-10 s) and back-azimuth window lengths (1.5 s to 30 min) before fixing the settings.
steps.quote: We test various thresholds for the STA/LTA algorithm and cross-correlation.

steps.action: Built VT and LP event catalogs for each sensor: 140 and 147 VT events, 488 and 1595 LP events.
steps.quote: The final VT event catalog includes a total of 140 events for the rotational sensor

steps.action: Compared catalogs, daily rates and SNRs between the rotational sensor, the seismometer and the INGV-OE catalog (VT SNR higher on the rotational sensor for 60% of events; LP SNR higher on the seismometer).
steps.quote: 97% of the events detected by the rotational sensor are also detected by the seismometer.

steps.action: Estimated VT event back azimuths from the horizontal rotation rates (2-5 Hz) and classified the events into four subclasses by stability.
steps.quote: We hence estimate the back azimuth using the horizontal components (Wassermann et al., 2020) of all VT events filtered from 2 to 5 Hz

steps.action: Compared VT back azimuths with INGV-OE hypocentres: consistent beyond 3 km, inconsistent for many events near the craters; derived a minimum magnitude versus distance.
steps.quote: For VT events with epicentral distance above 3 km and event depth of 4–6 km, the estimated back azimuths are in agreement

steps.action: Observed that LP events appear mainly on the vertical rotational component, indicating SH-type wave motion.
steps.quote: The LP event is in most cases only detected on the integrated vertical component of the rotational sensor hence indicating a dominant SH-type wave motion.

steps.action: Estimated LP back azimuths and SH phase velocities (500-1,000 m/s) by cross-correlating vertical rotation rate with transverse acceleration.
steps.quote: We estimate the back azimuth of the LP events using the vertical rotation rate and the transverse acceleration

steps.action: Compared LP back azimuths (160-220°) with crater directions and INGV-OE LP locations.
steps.quote: This is in broad agreement with the INGV-OE locations for LP events

steps.action: Observed that background tremor appears on the vertical rotational component and the east seismometer component, so it is SH-dominated.
steps.quote: Hence the persistent tremor wavefield is dominated by SH-type waves.

steps.action: Used the sustained strombolian activity of 8-13 September, met during the deployment, during which tremor broadened and gained SV-type energy.
steps.quote: From 8 to 13 September the tremor intensified and the frequency content is broad

steps.action: Estimated SH and SV tremor back azimuths in 30-min windows and tracked their migration through the activity change.
steps.quote: The SH-type wavefield of the tremor source migrates to 200–220° on 9 to 13 September

steps.action: Discussed catalog quality against the seismometer and the INGV-OE network: VT detection equal to the seismometer, LP detection lower, and the single station misses small or distant events.
steps.quote: Given the similar absolute number of events the single rotational sensor performs as good as the seismometer for VT events

steps.action: Excluded lower magnitude, lower SNR and different frequency content as explanations of the deviating VT back azimuths.
steps.quote: cannot be explained by lower magnitudes, lower SNR or different frequency content compared to Subclass 1 events

steps.action: Proposed ground properties, topography, short epicentral distance, the source and scattering by shallow heterogeneity or the Valle del Bove scarp as rival causes of the VT discrepancies.
steps.quote: might be caused by properties of the ground, the topography, the short epicentral distance, the source or scattered wave paths

steps.action: Excluded systematic squinting for VT events because no systematic back-azimuth offset appears for events in a similar area.
steps.quote: we conclude that the VT event location is not affected by squinting

steps.action: Compared LP frequency content and the pure SH wave type with earlier Etna polarization studies (Cannata 2009; Lokmer 2008; Saccorotti 2007; Falsaperla 2002).
steps.quote: We find that the SH-type waves compose the LP events on Etna.

steps.action: Proposed squinting, plumbing-system crossing, topography and local structure as causes of the 10-20° southward offset of LP and tremor back azimuths.
steps.quote: The back azimuths derived using the SH-type wavefield of LP events and tremor might hence be affected by squinting.

steps.action: Compared tremor back azimuths and their migration with INGV-OE amplitude-based tremor locations and with crater activity.
steps.quote: is consistent with the INGV-OE locations (Figure 7d)

steps.action: Checked SH phase velocities against independent DAS-derived phase velocity for an LP event on 27 August 2019, against MASW velocities and against published Etna velocities.
steps.quote: This comparison is beneficial since the consistent and independent results show that the method is reliable.

steps.action: Estimated tilt contamination of the seismometer from the integrated rotation of the largest VT event, unfiltered and in several frequency bands, and found it negligible except in the VLP band.
steps.quote: LP events, VT events and tremor recordings presented in this study are not affected by tilt.

steps.action: Kept the claim that a single rotational sensor detects events reliably and, with a seismometer, yields back azimuths, wave types and phase velocities on a volcano.
steps.quote: Back azimuth, wave types and phase velocities can now be extracted using merely two co-located instruments

tree.answer: VT events, LP events and tremor at Etna recorded on a 6C station
Rotation recorded directly; back azimuth and phase velocity inferred
Characterize rotational-sensor performance against a seismometer and the INGV-OE network
No rivals for the main claim; rivals only for back-azimuth discrepancies (scattering, topography, squinting, magnitude/SNR)
Partly: squinting predicts a systematic offset, which is absent for VT events
Conditions found: one month spanning weak and sustained strombolian activity
Thresholds and windows varied; tilt check; independent DAS phase velocity
Capability characterized, with limits for close VT events and LP detection

end.claim: A single rotational sensor detects VT and LP events reliably (97% of its LP detections also found by the seismometer) and, combined with a seismometer, yields back azimuths, wave types and phase velocities consistent with INGV-OE locations for distant VT events, LP events and tremor.

decisive_move.sentence: Without comparing the rotational-sensor catalogs and SNRs with the co-located seismometer and the INGV-OE catalog, the performance claim would not exist.

gates.evidence: Data were acquired to test a new sensor, not to test a stated hypothesis. The detection and back-azimuth results could have disagreed with the seismometer and INGV-OE, and partly did for VT events near the craters (p. 9, 14). Detection thresholds were chosen after the data were seen, to maximize overlap with the INGV-OE catalog (p. 4).

imports.item: Fiber-optic gyroscope based on the Sagnac effect (blueSeis-3A)
Quadrans fiber-optical gyro compass used for orientation
Distributed acoustic sensing on fiber-optic cable (cited DAS phase velocities)

novelty_claims.quote: using a newly developed 3C rotational sensor co-located with a 3C traditional seismometer on Etna
The rotational sensor is an unique instrument that allows us to separate waves in a wavefield such as SH and SV-waves.
Back azimuth, wave types and phase velocities can now be extracted using merely two co-located instruments

limits: Coded from the published PDF only. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded, and the Supporting Information (Figures S1-S4) was not available. The study uses a single station over one month. Detection thresholds were tuned to maximize overlap with the INGV-OE catalog, so the catalog comparison with INGV-OE is not independent of the tuning (inference). No formal uncertainty is reported for the phase velocities. Sub-claims at other statuses: LP events and background tremor are SH-dominated (regularity_in_range within this deployment); LP and tremor back azimuths point to the craters, with a 10-20° southward offset attributed to squinting or structure (best_explanation, the rivals untested); VT back azimuths are reliable beyond about 3 km but correct for only 31% of events near the craters (capability_characterized, with limits); SH phase velocities of 500-1,000 m/s for LP events and 300-400 m/s for tremor (estimate_with_resolution, no resolution stated). Rival causes of the VT discrepancies (scattering, topography, ground properties) are named but not tested. The paper does not report any failed or abandoned attempt.

disagreements.target: Yuan et al. (2020): SNR of rotation rates not larger than that of a seismometer
disagreements.support: In the 2-5 Hz band, 60% of VT events had higher SNR on the rotational sensor.
disagreements.quote: Yuan et al. (2020) do not confirm the larger SNR of rotation rates

disagreements.target: Cannata et al. (2009): LP wave motion of Rayleigh/SV type at distant stations, with a temporal change to P waves
disagreements.support: The rotational sensor records pure SH-type LP motion with no transition in wave type in 2019.
disagreements.quote: Here, we do not record a transition in wave type but a pure SH-type wave motion.

disagreements.target: Saccorotti et al. (2007): LP onsets dominated by radial motion
disagreements.support: Single-station wavefield separation shows SH-type motion only for LP events in this data set.
disagreements.quote: Saccorotti et al. (2007) conclude that the onset of the LP event recordings is at most stations dominated by radial wave motion

disagreements.target: INGV-OE earthquake catalog (EtnaRCSC) completeness for small near-crater events
disagreements.support: The station detects small (M < 1.3) VT events within 2 km that are absent from the INGV-OE catalog.
disagreements.quote: Until 2019, INGV-OE earthquake catalog did not include this [...] .

disagreements.target: INGV-OE amplitude-based tremor locations in early September
disagreements.support: The small back-azimuth discrepancy is attributed to radiation-pattern effects on amplitude-based location.
disagreements.quote: The slight discrepancy in back azimuth in early September might be caused by the radiation pattern on Etna

disagreements.target: Bean et al. (2014): shallow velocities giving Rayleigh velocities of 855 m/s
disagreements.support: The LP phase velocities found here agree with the lower velocities of Zuccarello et al. (2016) rather than those of Bean et al. (2014).
disagreements.quote: The velocities resolved by Zuccarello et al. (2016) are lower than the ones by Bean et al. (2014) and consistent with the here estimated

alternatives_considered.chosen: STA/LTA windows of 12/48 s for LP and 10/50 s for VT events
STA/LTA thresholds 2 (VT) and 2.8 (LP); cross-correlation thresholds 0.3 (VT) and 0.8 (LP)
alternatives_considered.reason: highest overlap with the INGV-OE catalog without an excessive amount of false picks

alternatives_considered.chosen: Final catalog = events in both the STA/LTA and the cross-correlation catalog
alternatives_considered.reason: reduces the number of false triggers

alternatives_considered.alternatives: full LP (0.5-5 Hz) and VLP bands
alternatives_considered.reason: to detect them more reliably in the seismometer and rotational sensor data

alternatives_considered.alternatives: 2-5 Hz band used for SNR and back azimuth

alternatives_considered.chosen: SNR windows of 4 s (VT) and 6 s (LP)
Short back-azimuth windows (1.5 s VT, 5 s LP); 30 min for tremor
alternatives_considered.alternatives: window lengths from 1.5 s to 30 min
alternatives_considered.reason: extract single phase arrivals and minimize scattering; tremor windows consistent with INGV-OE processing

alternatives_considered.chosen: Horizontal rotation rates for VT back azimuths; vertical rotation rate with transverse acceleration for LP events
alternatives_considered.reason: higher amplitude and SNR on the horizontal components for VT events; dominant SH-wave content for LP events

alternatives_considered.chosen: Discard SV-wave tremor back azimuths before 8 September
alternatives_considered.reason: low energy in the SV wavefield
